statement:
% P05.2 one-vertex orthogonality classification, live integration.

For this statement, $\mathrm{PA}_{\mathbf R}(\mathbf X)$ denotes the
continuous functions that are affine with arbitrary real slope and
constant on every face of some finite rational polyhedral structure.  This
is the real scalar extension of the lattice piecewise-affine class.  A
polyhedral convex combination is a finite barycentric combination
$x=\sum_j a_jx_j$ for which, on some common refinement, there are faces
$\tau$ and $\sigma_j$ with $x\in\tau$, $x_j\in\sigma_j$, and
$\tau\preceq\sigma_j$ for every $j$.  The envelope is
\[
 P_\gamma(u):=\sup\{\psi:\ \psi\leq\gamma+u,\quad
   \psi\in\mathrm{PC}(\mathbf X),\quad
   \psi\leq\gamma+O(1)\}.
\]
The proof of the one-dimensional envelope statement in
\cite[Proposition~6.13]{BMPS26} is an argument with real affine functions
and gives
$P_\gamma(u)\in\mathrm{PA}_{\mathbf R}(\mathbf X)\cap
\mathrm{PC}(\mathbf X)$ on the same finite structure whenever
$u\in\mathrm{PA}_{\mathbf R,b}(\mathbf X)$.  For such a function, write
$\MA_{\mathrm{poly},\mathbf R}(f):=\Delta f$, where the
one-dimensional Laplacian uses the primitive integral-affine coordinate
and the balancing weight on each edge.  This is the real-linear extension
of the source's one-dimensional intersection formula
\cite[Definition~6.15 and Proposition~6.17]{BMPS26}.
We say that $(\mathbf X,\gamma)$ has real-polyhedral orthogonality if, for
every $u\in\mathrm{PA}_{\mathbf R,b}(\mathbf X)$,
\[
 \int_{\mathbf X}
 \bigl(P_\gamma(u)-(\gamma+u)\bigr)
 \MA_{\mathrm{poly},\mathbf R}(P_\gamma(u))=0.
\]

The real scalar extension is essential here.  If Definition~2.28 of
\cite{BMPS26} is read literally with integral slopes, take
$\mathbf X=\mathbf R$, $\gamma(x)=|x|$, and
\[
 u(x)=
 \begin{cases}
  0,&x\leq1,\\
  1-x,&1\leq x\leq2,\\
  -1,&x\geq2.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then $u$ has integral slopes, but its envelope is
\[
 P_\gamma(u)(x)=
 \begin{cases}
  -x,&x\leq0,\\
  x/2,&0\leq x\leq2,\\
  x-1,&x\geq2.
 \end{cases}
\]
Indeed, the displayed function is an admissible convex minorant, while
the chord from $(0,0)$ to $(2,1)$ bounds every competitor on $[0,2]$ and
the obstacle gives the bound elsewhere.  Thus the literal integral-slope
class is not closed under these envelopes; the result below concerns the
explicitly stated real-polyhedral repair.

\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:frontier-polyhedral-one-vertex-convexity}
Let
\[
 \mathbf X=\bigcup_{i=1}^{r}\mathbf R_{\geq0}u_i
 \subset N_{\mathbf R}
\]
be the union of distinct rational rays with primitive generators $u_i$, put
\[
 K:=\left\{\lambda\in\mathbf R_{\geq0}^{r}:\
       \sum_{i=1}^{r}\lambda_i u_i=0\right\},
\]
and let $f$ be continuous and real-piecewise-affine on every ray.  If $s_i$
is the outgoing slope of $f$ at the origin along $u_i$, then $f$ is
polyhedrally convex if and only if every ray restriction is convex and
\[
                    \sum_i\lambda_i s_i\geq0
                    \quad\text{for every }\lambda\in K.
\]
If the ray $\mathbf R_{\geq0}u_i$ has balancing weight $w_i$, then
\[
             \MA_{\mathrm{poly},\mathbf R}(f)\{0\}=\sum_iw_i s_i.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:frontier-polyhedral-one-vertex-orthogonality}
Let
$
 \mathbf X=\bigcup_{i=1}^{r}\mathbf R_{\geq0}u_i
$
be a one-dimensional balanced rational fan with distinct primitive ray
directions $u_i$ and positive rational weights $w_i$ such that
$
 \sum_iw_i u_i=0
$.
Let $\gamma\in\mathrm{PA}_{\mathbf R}(\mathbf X)$ be polyhedrally convex,
affine on every ray, with outgoing slopes $g_i>0$.  Then
$(\mathbf X,\gamma)$ has real-polyhedral orthogonality if and only if
\[
 \dim K=1,
 \qquad
 K=\left\{\lambda\in\mathbf R_{\geq0}^{r}:\
       \sum_i\lambda_i u_i=0\right\}.
\]
Equivalently,
$
 \dim_{\mathbf R}\operatorname{span}\{u_1,\ldots,u_r\}=r-1
$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:frontier-polyhedral-one-vertex-bounded-shift}
In the setting of
\Cref{thm:frontier-polyhedral-one-vertex-orthogonality}, let $\gamma$ be
an arbitrary real-piecewise-affine polyhedrally convex reference positive at
infinity, without assuming that it is affine on each whole ray.  Thus
$\gamma$ is defined on a finite rational subdivision of the fan.  Then
$(\mathbf X,\gamma)$ has real-polyhedral orthogonality if and only if
$\dim K=1$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{example}
\label{ex:frontier-polyhedral-nonsaturated-tripod}
In $N=\mathbf Z^2$, take
\[
 u_1=(1,0),\qquad u_2=(1,2),\qquad u_3=(-3,-2),
 \qquad (w_1,w_2,w_3)=(2,1,1).
\]
The ray directions are primitive, their weighted sum is zero, and their
real span has rank two.  The lattice they generate has index two in $N$,
since the absolute values of the three pairwise determinants are $2,2,4$.
Thus the vertex is not polyhedrally smooth in the lattice sense, whereas
\Cref{cor:frontier-polyhedral-one-vertex-bounded-shift} gives
real-polyhedral orthogonality for every real-piecewise-affine
polyhedrally convex reference positive at infinity on this fan.
\end{example}

% P05.2 local rank-one graph orthogonality candidate, 25 September 2026.

Let $\mathbf X$ be a one-dimensional balanced rational polyhedral space,
and fix a finite rational polyhedral structure $\Pi$ carrying its balancing
cycle.  For a vertex $v\in\Pi^{(0)}$, write $E(v)$ for the incident edges,
$u_{e/v}$ for the primitive outgoing integral direction of $e$ at $v$, and
$w_e>0$ for the balancing weight of $e$.  Put
\[
 K_v:=\left\{\lambda\in\mathbf R_{\geq0}^{E(v)}:\
             \sum_{e\in E(v)}\lambda_eu_{e/v}=0\right\}.
\]
The local weight vector $w_v=(w_e)_{e\in E(v)}$ belongs to the relative
interior of $K_v$.

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:frontier-polyhedral-local-rank-one-graph}
Assume that $\dim K_v=1$ for every vertex $v\in\Pi^{(0)}$.  Let
$\gamma\in\mathrm{PA}_{\mathbf R}(\mathbf X)\cap
\mathrm{PC}(\mathbf X)$ be positive at infinity.  Then
$(\mathbf X,\gamma)$ has real-polyhedral orthogonality: for every
$u\in\mathrm{PA}_{\mathbf R,b}(\mathbf X)$,
\[
 \int_{\mathbf X}
 \bigl(P_\gamma(u)-(\gamma+u)\bigr)
 \MA_{\mathrm{poly},\mathbf R}(P_\gamma(u))=0.
\]
The conclusion allows bounded edges and cycles in the underlying graph.
It depends only on the local cones $K_v$ and is unchanged by subdividing
$\Pi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:frontier-polyhedral-trivalent-graph}
Every one-dimensional balanced rational polyhedral space admitting a finite
structure whose vertices have valence at most three satisfies the conclusion
of \Cref{thm:frontier-polyhedral-local-rank-one-graph} for every
real-piecewise-affine polyhedrally convex reference positive at infinity.
In particular, lattice saturation and the absence of bounded cycles are not
required.
\end{corollary}

The theorem is a sufficient criterion, not a converse.  At a vertex with
$\dim K_v>1$, the one-vertex construction gives a local noncontact mass
mechanism, but extending that germ through all bounded edges while retaining
global polyhedral convexity and the prescribed growth is a separate
realizability problem.

% P05.2 one-dimensional graph accessibility classification, 25 September 2026.

Continue with the finite one-dimensional balanced rational polyhedral
structure $\Pi$ and the local relation cones $K_v$ above.  We may insert one
bivalent vertex in every component without a vertex.  This does not change
any original relation cone or the orthogonality problem.

\begin{definition}
\label{def:frontier-polyhedral-mass-accessible}
Let $\gamma\in\mathrm{PA}_{\mathbf R}(\mathbf X)\cap
\mathrm{PC}(\mathbf X)$.  A vertex $v\in\Pi^{(0)}$ is
$\gamma$-mass-accessible if there is a function
\[
 \varphi\in\mathrm{PA}_{\mathbf R}(\mathbf X)\cap
 \mathrm{PC}(\mathbf X),
 \qquad
 \varphi-\gamma\in\mathrm{PA}_{\mathbf R,b}(\mathbf X),
\]
such that
\[
 \MA_{\mathrm{poly},\mathbf R}(\varphi)\{v\}
 =\sum_{e\in E(v)}w_es_{v,e}(\varphi)>0.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:frontier-polyhedral-accessible-mass-obstruction}
Suppose that $\dim K_v>1$ and that $v$ is
$\gamma$-mass-accessible.  Then $(\mathbf X,\gamma)$ does not have
real-polyhedral orthogonality.  More precisely, there is a bounded
real-piecewise-affine obstacle $u$ such that
\[
 \int_{\mathbf X}
 \bigl(P_\gamma(u)-(\gamma+u)\bigr)
 \MA_{\mathrm{poly},\mathbf R}(P_\gamma(u))<0.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:frontier-polyhedral-graph-orthogonality-classification}
Let $\mathbf X$ be a one-dimensional balanced rational polyhedral space
admitting a finite structure $\Pi$, and let
$\gamma\in\mathrm{PA}_{\mathbf R}(\mathbf X)\cap
\mathrm{PC}(\mathbf X)$ be positive at infinity.  Then
$(\mathbf X,\gamma)$ has real-polyhedral orthogonality if and only if no
vertex $v$ with $\dim K_v>1$ is $\gamma$-mass-accessible.
\end{theorem}

The condition in
\Cref{thm:frontier-polyhedral-graph-orthogonality-classification} has a
finite edge-jet test.  For a bounded edge $e=[v,w]$, orient $e$ from $v$ to
$w$ and write $\ell_e>0$ for its integral-affine length.  For an unbounded
edge $e$ incident to $v$, let $r_e$ be the slope of $\gamma$ in its
eventual primitive direction.

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:frontier-polyhedral-edge-jet-accessibility}
Choose one real number $H_v$ for every vertex and one real number $s_{v,e}$
for every vertex--edge incidence.  These numbers are the vertex values and
outgoing vertex slopes of some
\[
 \varphi\in\mathrm{PA}_{\mathbf R}(\mathbf X)\cap
 \mathrm{PC}(\mathbf X),
 \qquad
 \varphi-\gamma\in\mathrm{PA}_{\mathbf R,b}(\mathbf X),
\]
if and only if the following conditions hold.
\begin{enumerate}
 \item For every vertex $v$ and every $\lambda\in K_v$,
 \[
             \sum_{e\in E(v)}\lambda_es_{v,e}\geq0.
 \]
 \item For every bounded edge $e=[v,w]$, put
 \[
             d_e:=\frac{H_w-H_v}{\ell_e}.
 \]
 Then either
 \[
        s_{v,e}=d_e=-s_{w,e},
 \]
 or
 \[
        s_{v,e}<d_e<-s_{w,e}.
 \]
 \item For every unbounded edge $e$ incident to $v$,
 \[
                       s_{v,e}\leq r_e.
 \]
\end{enumerate}
Consequently a vertex $v$ is $\gamma$-mass-accessible if and only if this
finite system has a solution with
\[
                    \sum_{e\in E(v)}w_es_{v,e}>0.
\]
It is enough in the first condition to test the finitely many extreme rays
of $K_v$; after choosing one of the two alternatives on every bounded edge,
accessibility is a finite linear feasibility problem with weak and strict
inequalities.
\end{proposition}

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:frontier-polyhedral-reference-mass-obstruction}
If $\dim K_v>1$ and
$\MA_{\mathrm{poly},\mathbf R}(\gamma)\{v\}>0$ at some vertex $v$, then
$(\mathbf X,\gamma)$ fails real-polyhedral orthogonality.  In particular,
if the reference has positive vertex mass at every vertex with
$\dim K_v>1$, then real-polyhedral orthogonality holds if and only if
$\dim K_v=1$ at every vertex.
\end{corollary}
proof:
% P05.2 one-vertex orthogonality classification proof, live integration.

\begin{proof}[\Cref{lem:frontier-polyhedral-one-vertex-convexity}]
At a point in the relative interior of a ray, the incident-face condition
in the definition of a polyhedral convex combination forces all of its
points to lie on that ray.  The defining inequality is therefore ordinary
one-variable convexity.  At the origin,
let $x_i(t_{ij})=t_{ij}u_i$ be the points occurring in a polyhedral convex
combination, with coefficients $a_{ij}\geq0$ whose sum is one, and set
$
 \lambda_i:=\sum_j a_{ij}t_{ij}
$.
The barycentre condition gives
$
 \sum_i\lambda_i u_i=0
$, so $\lambda\in K$.  Convexity on each ray gives
\[
 f(x_i(t_{ij}))\geq f(0)+s_i t_{ij};
\]
after multiplication by $a_{ij}$ and summation, the required Jensen
inequality follows from $\lambda\cdot s\geq0$.

Conversely, fix $\lambda\in K\setminus\{0\}$, choose a small positive
rational $t$ on which every ray restriction is affine, and use the points
$x_i(t)$ with coefficients
$
 \lambda_i/\sum_j\lambda_j
$.
They form a polyhedral convex combination with barycentre zero.  Its Jensen
inequality gives $\lambda\cdot s\geq0$.  This proves the convexity
criterion.  Since each $u_i$ is primitive, $t$ is the integral-affine
coordinate on its ray.  The one-dimensional Laplacian formula for the
polyhedral Monge--Amp\`ere measure therefore assigns to the origin the
weighted sum of these normalized outgoing slopes.  This gives the last
formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[\Cref{thm:frontier-polyhedral-one-vertex-orthogonality}]
The positive vector $w=(w_i)$ belongs to the relative interior of $K$.
Consequently
\[
 \dim K=r-\dim_{\mathbf R}\operatorname{span}\{u_1,\ldots,u_r\},
\]
which proves the final equivalence.

Assume first that $K=\mathbf R_{\geq0}w$.  The definition of
real-polyhedral orthogonality quantifies exactly over bounded
real-piecewise-affine obstacles, so fix one such
$u$ and put
\[
             a:=\gamma+u,
             \qquad f:=P_\gamma(u).
\]
The one-dimensional real-affine envelope statement quoted above makes $f$
real-piecewise-affine and polyhedrally convex on a common finite subdivision of
the rays.  Its Monge--Amp\`ere measure is consequently supported on the
vertices of that subdivision.  No approximation or larger obstacle class
is involved in the definition of orthogonality.

Let $x$ be an interior subdivision vertex with positive mass.  On a small
interval $[a_0,b_0]$ around $x$, containing no other subdivision vertex,
the left and right slopes of $f$ satisfy $m_-<m_+$.  If $f(x)<a(x)$,
then $a-f$ has a positive lower bound on a smaller such interval.  Raise
$f(x)$ by $\delta>0$, retain the values at $a_0,b_0$, and interpolate
linearly.  When $\delta$ is smaller than the obstacle gap and
\[
 \delta\bigl((x-a_0)^{-1}+(b_0-x)^{-1}\bigr)<m_+-m_-,
\]
the two new inner slopes remain ordered.  At $a_0$ the inner slope has
increased, and at $b_0$ it has decreased, so convexity is preserved there
as well.  The modified function is continuous and polyhedrally convex,
differs boundedly from $f$, and stays below the obstacle.  Thus it is a
larger admissible envelope competitor (competitors need not themselves be
piecewise affine), a contradiction.  Hence every positive atom in the
interior of a ray is a contact point.

At the origin, choose $\rho>0$ so that the segments
$[0,\rho]u_i$ contain no other subdivision vertex, and let $s_i$ be the
outgoing slopes of $f$ there.  If the vertex mass
$
 m=\sum_iw_i s_i
$
is positive and $f(0)<a(0)$, shrink $\rho$ so that $a-f$ has a
positive lower bound on the resulting compact star.  Raise $f(0)$ by
$\delta>0$ and interpolate to the unchanged values $f(\rho u_i)$.  The
new outgoing slopes are $s_i-\delta/\rho$, and for sufficiently small
$\delta$,
\[
 \sum_iw_i(s_i-\delta/\rho)
       =m-\frac{\delta}{\rho}\sum_iw_i>0.
\]
Because $K=\mathbf R_{\geq0}w$,
\Cref{lem:frontier-polyhedral-one-vertex-convexity} preserves polyhedral
convexity at the origin.  Along each ray the modified slope increases back
to $s_i$ at $\rho u_i$, so raywise convexity is also preserved.  Taking
$\delta$ below the obstacle gap gives a larger admissible competitor,
again a contradiction.  Thus every positive atom of
$\MA_{\mathrm{poly},\mathbf R}(f)$ lies in the contact set $\{f=a\}$, and the
orthogonality integral vanishes.

Now suppose that $\dim K>1$.  Choose an extreme ray
$\mathbf R_{\geq0}\lambda$ of $K$.  Its support
$
 S:=\{i:\lambda_i>0\}
$
is a proper subset of $\{1,\ldots,r\}$: a vector of full support belongs
to the relative interior of $K$, and an extreme ray can meet that
relative interior only when $K$ is one-dimensional.  After temporarily
subtracting $\gamma(0)$, define
\[
 f(tu_i):=
 \begin{cases}
   g_i\max\{t-2,0\},&i\in S,\\
   g_i t,&i\notin S.
 \end{cases}
\]
Its outgoing slopes are zero on $S$ and $g_i>0$ off $S$, so
\Cref{lem:frontier-polyhedral-one-vertex-convexity} makes $f$
polyhedrally convex.  It is real-piecewise-affine, and
$f-\gamma$ is bounded because its eventual slope on every ray is $g_i$.
After restoring the constant $\gamma(0)$, its vertex mass is
\[
             \MA_{\mathrm{poly},\mathbf R}(f)\{0\}
             =\sum_{i\notin S}w_i g_i>0.
\]

Set $b(tu_i):=\max\{1-t,0\}$ and $u:=f+b-\gamma$.  Then $u$ is
bounded and real-piecewise-affine, and $f$ is a competitor below
$\gamma+u=f+b$.  If $h\leq f+b$ is any other polyhedrally convex
competitor, the points $u_i=x_i(1)$, for $i\in S$, have a balanced
convex combination with coefficients
$
 \lambda_i/\sum_{j\in S}\lambda_j
$.
Since $b(u_i)=0$ and $f(u_i)=f(0)$ on $S$, polyhedral convexity gives
\[
 h(0)\leq
 \sum_{i\in S}\frac{\lambda_i}{\sum_{j\in S}\lambda_j}h(u_i)
 \leq f(0).
\]
On every segment $[0,u_i]$, ordinary convexity and the endpoint bounds
give $h\leq f$, because $f$ is affine there.  For $t\geq1$ the bump
$b$ vanishes, so the obstacle inequality gives $h\leq f$ directly.
Therefore $P_\gamma(u)=f$.

The only positive masses of $f$ occur at the origin and at $2u_i$ for
$i\in S$.  The bump $b$ equals one at the origin and vanishes at all
the latter points.  Hence
\[
 \int_{\mathbf X}
 \bigl(P_\gamma(u)-(\gamma+u)\bigr)
 \MA_{\mathrm{poly},\mathbf R}(P_\gamma(u))
 =-\sum_{i\notin S}w_i g_i<0.
\]
Orthogonality fails, proving the converse.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[\Cref{cor:frontier-polyhedral-one-vertex-bounded-shift}]
On each ray, let $g_i>0$ be the eventual slope of $\gamma$, and define
the raywise affine reference
\[
                    \gamma_\infty(tu_i):=\gamma(0)+g_i t.
\]
The positivity of the slopes and
\Cref{lem:frontier-polyhedral-one-vertex-convexity} show that
$\gamma_\infty$ is polyhedrally convex and positive at infinity.  Since
$\gamma$ has only finitely many affine pieces, the difference
$\gamma-\gamma_\infty$ is bounded and real-piecewise-affine.  Put
$\delta:=\gamma-\gamma_\infty$.  The two bounded-growth conditions agree,
and the defining competitor sets give the bounded reference-shift identity
\[
                  P_\gamma(u)=P_{\gamma_\infty}(u+\delta).
\]
Translation by $\delta$ is a bijection of the bounded real-piecewise-affine
obstacles.  For corresponding obstacles the envelope, its
Monge--Amp\`ere measure, and the difference between envelope and obstacle
are identical, so the two orthogonality integrals agree.  This also proves
directly the instance of
\Cref{prop:frontier-polyhedral-bounded-reference-shift} used here.  Apply
\Cref{thm:frontier-polyhedral-one-vertex-orthogonality}.
\end{proof}

% P05.2 local rank-one graph orthogonality proof, 25 September 2026.

\begin{proof}[\Cref{thm:frontier-polyhedral-local-rank-one-graph}]
Fix $u\in\mathrm{PA}_{\mathbf R,b}(\mathbf X)$, put
\[
 a:=\gamma+u,
 \qquad
 f:=P_\gamma(u),
 \qquad
 \mu:=\MA_{\mathrm{poly},\mathbf R}(f).
\]
After a common finite refinement, $a$ is real-piecewise affine.  The
real-affine proof of the one-dimensional envelope statement in
\cite[Proposition~6.13]{BMPS26} gives
$f\in\mathrm{PA}_{\mathbf R}(\mathbf X)\cap\mathrm{PC}(\mathbf X)$
on that refinement.  Consequently $\mu$ is a nonnegative atomic measure
supported at its vertices.  A newly inserted vertex in the interior of an
old edge has two opposite primitive directions and equal inherited weights,
so its cone of nonnegative balancing relations is one-dimensional.  Thus the
hypothesis persists under the refinement.

We show that every point carrying positive $\mu$-mass lies in the contact
set $\{f=a\}$.  Let $v$ be a vertex of the refined structure, let $s_e$ be
the outgoing slope of $f$ along $e\in E(v)$, and suppose
\[
 m:=\mu\{v\}=\sum_{e\in E(v)}w_es_e>0,
 \qquad
 f(v)<a(v).
\]
For every incident edge choose a point $x_e$ at integral-affine distance
$\rho_e>0$ from $v$, so close that the open segment $(v,x_e)$ contains no
other vertex and $f$ is affine on $[v,x_e]$.  The continuous function
$a-f$ is positive at $v$, hence is bounded below by a positive constant on
a sufficiently small closed star; choose the points inside that star.

For $\delta>0$, define $f_\delta$ by raising the value at $v$ from $f(v)$
to $f(v)+\delta$, interpolating affinely from that new value to the unchanged
value $f(x_e)$ on every segment $[v,x_e]$, and leaving $f$ unchanged
elsewhere.  Choose $\delta$ smaller than the obstacle gap and so small that
\[
 0<\delta<
 \frac{m}{\sum_{e\in E(v)}w_e/\rho_e}.
\]
The new outgoing slope at $v$ along $e$ is
$s_e-\delta/\rho_e$.  Since $K_v=\mathbf R_{\geq0}w_v$, the local
polyhedral-convexity inequalities at $v$ reduce to the single inequality
\[
 \sum_e w_e\left(s_e-\frac{\delta}{\rho_e}\right)
 =m-\delta\sum_e\frac{w_e}{\rho_e}>0.
\]
At $x_e$, the slope on the segment from $v$ has decreased by
$\delta/\rho_e$ in the coordinate pointing away from $v$ and then returns
to the old slope.  Ordinary one-variable convexity is therefore preserved.
All other local convexity inequalities are unchanged.  The local
one-dimensional slope criterion, equivalently
\cite[Definitions~3.1--3.3 and Lemma~3.4]{BMPS26}, now shows that
$f_\delta$ is polyhedrally convex.

Moreover $f_\delta\leq a$, and $f_\delta-f$ has compact support, so
$f_\delta\leq\gamma+O(1)$.  Hence $f_\delta$ is an admissible competitor
for $P_\gamma(u)$ and satisfies $f_\delta(v)>f(v)$, contradicting the
definition of the envelope.  We conclude that
\[
 \operatorname{supp}\mu\subseteq\{f=a\}.
\]
The integrand $f-a$ vanishes on the support of the nonnegative atomic
measure $\mu$, and the asserted orthogonality integral is therefore zero.
The argument is local at the vertices and never removes a bounded edge or
cuts a graph cycle, proving the last two assertions.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[\Cref{cor:frontier-polyhedral-trivalent-graph}]
Balancing excludes a one-valent vertex.  At a two-valent vertex the two
primitive outgoing directions are opposite, and its positive balancing
relation spans $K_v$.  At a three-valent vertex, the three distinct outgoing
rays cannot all lie in a one-dimensional vector subspace.  Their span
therefore has dimension two, and the kernel of the direction map
$\mathbf R^3\to N_{\mathbf R}$ is one-dimensional.  Its positive balancing
vector spans $K_v$.  Thus every vertex satisfies $\dim K_v=1$, and
\Cref{thm:frontier-polyhedral-local-rank-one-graph} applies.
\end{proof}

% P05.2 one-dimensional graph accessibility classification proof, 25 September 2026.

\begin{proof}[\Cref{lem:frontier-polyhedral-accessible-mass-obstruction}]
Choose $\varphi$ as in
\Cref{def:frontier-polyhedral-mass-accessible}.  Let
$s=(s_e)_{e\in E(v)}$ be its outgoing slope vector at $v$, let
$w=(w_e)_{e\in E(v)}$, and put
\[
                         m:=w\mathbin{\cdot}s>0.
\]
The local convexity criterion gives
$\lambda\mathbin{\cdot}s\geq0$ for every $\lambda\in K_v$.

Let $L_v$ be the linear span of $K_v$.  Since $\dim K_v>1$ and
$w\mathbin{\cdot}s>0$, choose a positive rational vector
$c=(c_e)_{e\in E(v)}$ such that the restrictions of $c$ and $s$ to $L_v$
are not proportional.  Multiplying $c$ by a sufficiently large positive
rational number, choose points $x_e$ at integral-affine distance
$\rho_e=c_e^{-1}$ from $v$ such that every segment $[v,x_e]$ contains no
other vertex and $\varphi$ is affine on it.  The slice
\[
                       B_c:=\{\lambda\in K_v:\lambda\mathbin{\cdot}c=1\}
\]
is nonempty and compact.  Set
\[
                       \tau:=\min_{\lambda\in B_c}
                       \lambda\mathbin{\cdot}s\geq0.
\]

Raise $\varphi(v)$ by $\tau$, interpolate affinely to the unchanged values
$\varphi(x_e)$, and leave $\varphi$ unchanged off the closed star.  Denote
the resulting function by $\widetilde\varphi$.  Its outgoing slope vector
at $v$ is
\[
                         \widetilde s=s-\tau c.
\]
The definition of $\tau$ gives
$\lambda\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde s\geq0$ for every $\lambda\in K_v$,
and a minimizer $\lambda^0\in B_c$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
                  \lambda^0\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde s=0.
                  \label{eq:frontier-polyhedral-supporting-relation}
\end{equation}
At each $x_e$ the modified slope increases back to the old slope, so
one-variable convexity is preserved.  All other local inequalities are
unchanged.  Thus $\widetilde\varphi$ is polyhedrally convex and remains
$\gamma$-bounded.

Its mass at $v$ is still positive.  This is immediate when $\tau=0$.
If $\tau>0$, the linear functional
$\lambda\mapsto\lambda\mathbin{\cdot}s$ is nonconstant on $B_c$ by the
choice of $c$.  The point
$w/(w\mathbin{\cdot}c)$ lies in the relative interior of $B_c$, so its
value is strictly larger than the minimum.  Hence
\begin{equation}
 \frac{w\mathbin{\cdot}s}{w\mathbin{\cdot}c}>\tau,
 \qquad
 w\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde s>0.
 \label{eq:frontier-polyhedral-positive-projected-mass}
\end{equation}

Let $b$ be the real-piecewise-affine function which is one at $v$, zero at
every $x_e$, affine on $[v,x_e]$, and zero off the closed star.  Put
\[
                         a:=\widetilde\varphi+b,
                         \qquad
                         u:=a-\gamma.
\]
Then $u$ is bounded and real-piecewise affine, and
$\widetilde\varphi$ is an admissible competitor for $P_\gamma(u)$.

Let $h\leq a$ be any polyhedrally convex envelope competitor and put
\[
 C:=\sum_e\frac{\lambda^0_e}{\rho_e},
 \qquad
 \alpha_e:=\frac{\lambda^0_e/\rho_e}{C}.
\]
Because $x_e=v+\rho_eu_{e/v}$ and $\lambda^0\in K_v$, the points $x_e$
with coefficients $\alpha_e$ form a polyhedral convex combination with
barycentre $v$.  Since $b(x_e)=0$, polyhedral convexity and
\eqref{eq:frontier-polyhedral-supporting-relation} give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 h(v)
 &\leq\sum_e\alpha_eh(x_e)
 \leq\sum_e\alpha_e\widetilde\varphi(x_e)\\
 &=\widetilde\varphi(v)
   +\frac{1}{C}\sum_e\lambda^0_e\widetilde s_e
 =\widetilde\varphi(v).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Taking the supremum over competitors and using the competitor
$\widetilde\varphi$ shows that, for $P:=P_\gamma(u)$,
\[
                         P(v)=\widetilde\varphi(v),
                         \qquad
                         P\geq\widetilde\varphi.
\]

The one-dimensional real-affine envelope theorem makes $P$
real-piecewise affine.  Since $P-\widetilde\varphi$ is nonnegative and
vanishes at $v$, every outgoing slope of $P$ at $v$ is at least the
corresponding slope of $\widetilde\varphi$.  By
\eqref{eq:frontier-polyhedral-positive-projected-mass},
\[
              \MA_{\mathrm{poly},\mathbf R}(P)\{v\}
              \geq w\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde s>0.
\]
At $v$ one has $P-a=-1$, while $P-a\leq0$ everywhere and
$\MA_{\mathrm{poly},\mathbf R}(P)$ is nonnegative.  Therefore
\[
 \int_{\mathbf X}(P-a)\MA_{\mathrm{poly},\mathbf R}(P)
 \leq-\MA_{\mathrm{poly},\mathbf R}(P)\{v\}<0.
\]
This is the required failure of orthogonality.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[\Cref{thm:frontier-polyhedral-graph-orthogonality-classification}]
If a higher-relation-rank vertex is $\gamma$-mass-accessible,
\Cref{lem:frontier-polyhedral-accessible-mass-obstruction} disproves
orthogonality.

Conversely, assume that no such vertex is accessible.  Fix
$u\in\mathrm{PA}_{\mathbf R,b}(\mathbf X)$, put
\[
                         a:=\gamma+u,
                         \qquad
                         P:=P_\gamma(u),
\]
and take a common finite refinement on which $a$ and $P$ are
real-piecewise affine.  Every new vertex in the interior of an old edge has
a one-dimensional relation cone.  At each original vertex with
$\dim K_v>1$, the envelope $P$ itself is a $\gamma$-bounded
polyhedrally convex real-piecewise-affine function.  Non-accessibility
therefore forces
\[
                    \MA_{\mathrm{poly},\mathbf R}(P)\{v\}=0.
\]

At every remaining vertex the relation cone is one-dimensional.  If such a
vertex had positive $P$-mass and were not in the contact set $\{P=a\}$, the
local tent perturbation from the proof of
\Cref{thm:frontier-polyhedral-local-rank-one-graph} would give a larger
admissible competitor.  Hence every positive atom of
$\MA_{\mathrm{poly},\mathbf R}(P)$ lies in $\{P=a\}$.  The integrand
$P-a$ vanishes on the support of this nonnegative atomic measure, proving
orthogonality.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[\Cref{prop:frontier-polyhedral-edge-jet-accessibility}]
Suppose first that $\varphi$ exists.  The local slope criterion gives the
first condition.  On an oriented bounded edge $e=[v,w]$, ordinary convexity
shows
\[
                    s_{v,e}\leq d_e\leq-s_{w,e}.
\]
If the two endpoint slopes differ, $\varphi$ is affine with the first slope
on a nontrivial interval next to $v$ and with the second slope on a
nontrivial interval next to $w$.  Its average slope is then strictly between
them.  This gives exactly the two alternatives in the second condition.  On
an unbounded edge, boundedness of $\varphi-\gamma$ forces the eventual slope
of $\varphi$ to be $r_e$, and convexity gives $s_{v,e}\leq r_e$.

Conversely, assume the three conditions.  On a bounded oriented edge, write
\[
                  p:=s_{v,e},
                  \qquad q:=-s_{w,e},
                  \qquad d:=d_e.
\]
In the equality case, use the affine function of slope $d$.  In the strict
case $p<d<q$, choose sufficiently small positive rational numbers
$a,c$ with $a+c<\ell_e$ such that
\[
                   m_e:=
                   \frac{\ell_ed-ap-cq}{\ell_e-a-c}
                   \quad\text{satisfies}\quad
                   p<m_e<q.
\]
Starting from $H_v$, use the successive slopes $p,m_e,q$ on the intervals
of lengths $a$, $\ell_e-a-c$, and $c$.  Their integral is
$\ell_ed=H_w-H_v$, so the resulting function has the prescribed endpoint
values and outgoing slopes and is convex.

On an unbounded edge, use the slope $s_{v,e}$ on an initial interval of
positive rational length and then the slope $r_e$; if the two slopes are
equal, use the affine function.  These edge functions glue continuously at
the prescribed vertex values.  They are convex in edge interiors, and the
first condition gives every local nonnegative-cycle inequality at every
vertex.  The one-dimensional local slope criterion therefore makes the
glued function $\varphi$ polyhedrally convex.  All new breakpoints occur at
rational integral-affine distances.  On every unbounded edge, $\varphi$ and
$\gamma$ have the same eventual slope, so their difference is bounded.
There are only finitely many remaining edges, proving
$\varphi-\gamma\in\mathrm{PA}_{\mathbf R,b}(\mathbf X)$.

The mass formula at $v$ is
$\sum_ew_es_{v,e}$, proving the accessibility criterion.  Each $K_v$ is a
finitely generated polyhedral cone, so its inequalities reduce to its
extreme rays.  The final finite-feasibility assertion follows by choosing,
for each bounded edge, either the equality branch or the strict branch.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[\Cref{cor:frontier-polyhedral-reference-mass-obstruction}]
The reference $\gamma$ itself witnesses $\gamma$-mass-accessibility at every
vertex where its mass is positive.  The first assertion follows from
\Cref{lem:frontier-polyhedral-accessible-mass-obstruction}.  If every
higher-rank vertex has positive reference mass, any such vertex therefore
precludes orthogonality.  If there is no higher-rank vertex,
\Cref{thm:frontier-polyhedral-local-rank-one-graph} gives orthogonality.
\end{proof}
